entry.note: Csw.dispatch_wsgi splits environ['QUERY_STRING'] into self.kvp (unquoted, values untouched); Csw.dispatch (about 300 lines, cut) lower-cases the keys via normalize_kvp, picks the Csw2 interface and calls its getrecords, which reads self.parent.kvp['constraint'] when constraintlanguage=CQL_TEXT on a GET request. dispatch_wsgi is kept in the slice so the request read is visible, but the dispatch hop between it and Csw2.getrecords is not, hence the stand-in

guards.note: CQL_TEXT branch. clean: cql2fes1(tmp, namespaces) then fes1.parse(...) produce constraint['where'] with :pvalueN placeholders and constraint['values'] holding the literals; any parse failure returns an exception report before the repository is queried. regressed: constraint['where'] = self.parent._cql_update_queryables_mappings(tmp, queryables) (plain str.replace of queryable names by column names) with empty values, i.e. the request text itself becomes the WHERE clause

new module in the clean commit (absent at the regressed commit): splits the CQL on and/or, requires each condition to be exactly 'property operator literal' with the operator taken from fes1 MODEL['ComparisonOperators'], and emits an ogc:Filter element tree; fes1.parse (pycsw/ogc/fes/fes1.py, unchanged, not in the slice) then maps the property name through the queryables dict (unknown name raises) and binds the literal as a parameter

sinks.note: self.session.query(self.dataset).filter(text(constraint['where'])).params(self._create_values(constraint['values'])) - SQLAlchemy text() runs the where string as literal SQL; .count() and .all() execute it

notes: Written at 2.3 (2026-10-04). Class sql (CWE-89), matching the advisory: the CQL_TEXT constraint of a GetRecords request becomes the text of a SQL WHERE clause. Modelled flow (CSW 2.0.2 KVP GET): QUERY_STRING -> Csw.dispatch_wsgi (self.kvp) -> Csw.dispatch (cut) -> Csw2.getrecords -> Csw._cql_update_queryables_mappings -> Repository.query -> filter(text(where)). Verified by reading both commits: at cd425019 the only processing of the constraint is str.replace of queryable names; at d83df944 the constraint goes through cql2fes1 and fes1.parse, where the property name must be a key of the queryables dict, the operator must be one of the fixed ComparisonOperators opvalues (otherwise fes1_predicate is unbound and the except branch returns an exception report), and the literal is appended to values and referenced as :pvalueN. Not executed: lxml/sqlalchemy are not installed here, so closure is established by code reading only. The same commit closes three parallel flows that are not modelled: Csw2._parse_constraint (POST csw:CqlText, reaching Repository.query and, through Csw2.transaction, Repository.update/delete), and the two equivalent sites in pycsw/ogc/csw/csw3.py (Csw3.getrecords, Csw3._parse_constraint). Injecting this event therefore reverts only the csw2.py GET site plus cql.py; csw3.py and _parse_constraint are outside the slice. SRU (pycsw/sru.py request_sru2csw) and OAI-PMH requests are rewritten into the same kvp with constraintlanguage=CQL_TEXT and reach the modelled site. The regression diff also carries the fix's second change in getrecords: the error text returned to the client ('Invalid query: %s' % err, which echoes the database error, versus 'Invalid query syntax' plus two debug log calls); it is part of the same upstream fix, not an unrelated hunk. After the fix Csw._cql_update_queryables_mappings is still defined but has no caller; it is kept in the slice because the regressed path calls it. Size: Csw2.getrecords alone is about 19 KB (request validation, the query, then response writing), so the clean slice is about 30 KB, over the 24 KB soft limit and under the hard limit; the function cannot be cut without removing the entry, guard and sink call site. fes1.parse (about 10 KB) is left out to stay near the limit; the clean slice shows the guard being called but not the parameter binding itself. Accepted dropped references: Csw.dispatch (the cut hop, see entry note), Csw._write_response (response output, called from dispatch_wsgi's early return), Csw2._write_acknowledgement and Csw2._write_record (response writers called from getrecords after the query, not on the flow).
